label: Diagram 5.2
caption: Diagram 5.2 Junction of compartment wall with roof | Cavities
description: A drawing headed "See paras 5.12 to 5.15" and captioned "Diagram 5.2 Junction of compartment wall with roof", in three parts. Part a, "ANY BUILDING OR COMPARTMENT", is a section of a compartment wall labelled "Wall" under a roof, with "1500mm" marked on each side of the wall over the roof covering. Notes say: the roof covering over this distance is to be designated BROOF(t4) rated on a deck of material of class A2-s3, d2 or better (roof covering and deck could be a composite structure, e.g. profiled steel cladding); double-skinned insulated roof sheeting should incorporate a band of material rated class A2-s3, d2 or better, at least 300mm wide, centred over the wall; if roof support members pass through the wall, fire protection to them for 1500mm on either side of the wall may be needed to delay distortion at the junction (see paragraph 5.9); and fire-stopping is to be carried up to the underside of the roof covering, e.g. roof tiles. Part b, "RESIDENTIAL (DWELLINGS) AND RESIDENTIAL (OTHER) A MAXIMUM OF 15M HIGH", shows the same arrangement with "1500mm" either side and a section line X–X. Its notes say: roof covering to be designated BROOF(t4) rated for at least this distance; boarding (used as a substrate) or timber tiling battens may be carried over the wall if fully bedded in mortar (or other no less suitable material) where over the wall; thermoplastic insulation materials should not be carried over the wall; double-skinned insulated roof sheeting with a thermoplastic core should incorporate a band of material of class A2-s3, d2 at least 300mm wide centred over the wall; sarking felt may also be carried over the wall; the same note on roof support members (see paragraph 5.9); and fire-stopping to be carried up to the underside of the roof covering, boarding or slab. "Section X–X" shows the pitched roof over masonry, with notes: roof covering to be designated BROOF(t4) rated for at least 1500mm either side of the wall; roofing battens and sarking felt may be carried over the wall; fire-stopping to be carried up to the underside of the roof covering above and below the sarking felt. NOTES: 1. Fire-stopping should be carried over the full thickness of the wall. 2. Fire-stopping should be extended into any eaves. 3. The compartment wall does not necessarily need to be constructed of masonry. Part c, "ANY BUILDING OR COMPARTMENT", shows the wall extended up through the roof between two roof coverings, with "At least 375mm" marked above the adjoining roof covering on each side (on the sloping side measured at right angles to the slope). Its text says the wall should be extended up through the roof for at least 375mm above the top surface of the adjoining roof covering, and where there is a height difference of at least 375mm between two roofs, or the roof coverings on either side are BROOF(t4) rated, the upstand or parapet above the highest roof may be reduced to 200mm.
first_draft:
A section drawing, part c., headed "ANY BUILDING OR COMPARTMENT", beneath the title "Diagram 5.2 Junction of compartment wall with roof". At the top edge a partial, cut-off line drawing of roof framing elements (rectangular members) is visible.

Below, a vertical grey rectangle labelled "Wall" stands in cross-section. To its left a sloping line descends to a horizontal line; both are labelled "Roof covering". To the right a horizontal line is likewise labelled "Roof covering". A vertical dimension arrow on the left of the wall, between the sloping roof line and the wall's top, reads "At least 375mm". A matching arrow on the right, between the wall's top and the horizontal roof covering, also reads "At least 375mm".

To the right of the diagram are two paragraphs of explanatory text stating the wall should extend up through the roof for at least 375 mm, and that this height may be reduced to 200 mm under certain conditions (a 375 mm height difference between roofs, or B ROOF (t4) rated coverings).

model_description:
A section drawing, part c., headed "ANY BUILDING OR COMPARTMENT", above the title "Diagram 5.2 Junction of compartment wall with roof" which is in a green band at the bottom. At the top edge a partial, cut-off line drawing of roof framing elements (rectangular members) is visible.

Below, a vertical grey rectangle labelled "Wall" stands in cross-section. To its left a sloping line descends towards the wall and is labelled "Roof covering". To the right a horizontal line extends from the wall and is labelled "Roof covering". A vertical dimension on the left, spanning the vertical height of the sloping roof section, reads "At least 375mm". A matching dimension on the right, between the wall's top and the horizontal roof covering, reads "At least 375mm".

To the right of the diagram are two paragraphs of explanatory text stating the wall should extend up through the roof for at least 375 mm, and that the height of the upstand/parapet wall above the highest roof may be reduced to 200 mm under certain conditions (a 375 mm height difference between roofs, or B ROOF (t4) rated coverings).
